# VULCAN Maintenance Report
**Asset:** HSM.F1.GBX01 | **Scenario:** SCN-038 | **Generated:** 2026-06-11
**Prepared by:** EDITH / VULCAN Agentic Maintenance Wizard

---

## 1. Diagnosis

Failure mode: **gear_tooth_fatigue_crack** [1]. The primary sensor flag is oil viscosity on JSR.HR.STD1.GBX01.OIL.VISC reading **216.601** (WARNING band; warn threshold 180, alarm threshold 265) [2]. The ML fault classifier currently reports NORMAL (P=0.9999) with zero probability of FAILURE [2] — however, this reading must not be used to defer action. Spall debris from a fatigue crack contaminates the oil and can generate a false-normal classifier output before a catastrophic fracture event. The chip-detector / ferrographic signal is the decisive trigger, not the probabilistic classifier, per the SOP governing this asset [8].

---

## 2. Root Cause

Tooth-root fatigue crack initiated by a prior high-torque cobble event [1][4]. The cobble event induced cyclic overloading at the tooth root, propagating a subsurface fatigue crack. Chunky spall debris is now present in the oil circuit [1][4]. Under AGMA 2101-D04 failure taxonomy, this classifies as tooth-root fracture — an immediate-stop condition [8].

---

## 3. Remaining Useful Life

ML RUL estimate: **~632 cycles (≈26.3 days)** [3]. Anomaly score: 0.4898 (below anomaly threshold; is_anomaly = False) [3]. RUL band: **monitor** [3][5].

> ⚠️ **Caution:** RUL projections assume gradual degradation. Gear tooth fatigue crack propagation is non-linear — fracture can occur abruptly well before the modelled horizon. The SOP classifies this failure mode as a **no-deferral immediate-stop event** once chip detector alarms or spall is confirmed [8]. Do not rely on the 26-day estimate for scheduling deferrals.

---

## 4. Risk Classification

**RISK: HIGH — Score 7/10** [5]

| Factor | Contribution |
|---|---|
| Process criticality (Criticality-1 asset) | +3 [5] |
| Safety class P2 | +2 [5] |
| ML P(failure) = 0.00 | +0 [5] |
| RUL band = monitor | +0 [5] |
| Key spare GEAR-WHL-M20 out-of-stock, 36-week lead | +2 [5] |

The spare-stock situation is the critical risk amplifier. The gear wheel is a custom large-module M20+ component with a 36-week OEM lead time [5][6]. If fracture occurs before the spare arrives, unplanned downtime extends by the full procurement lead.

---

## 5. Recommended Actions (Option B — Major Overhaul)

Execute in sequence; no step is deferrable once this order is raised [4][6]:

1. **Immediate controlled stop** — no deferral permitted [4][6][8].
2. **Remove gearbox via crane to repair bay** [4][6].
3. Inspect all gear teeth under workshop lighting; photograph every tooth, classify damage per **AGMA 2101-D04** (pitting / spalling / micro-pitting / scuffing / tooth-root fracture) [10].
4. Remove damaged gear wheel using hydraulic press; if shrink-fit, apply localised induction heat to gear boss only — **no direct flame** (annealing risk to shaft) [10].
5. Inspect gear seat on shaft for fretting, wear, or corrosion; measure seat diameter vs. OEM tolerance [10].
6. **Replace gear wheel + full bearing set** (replace bearings as an opportunity item regardless of apparent condition — bearing replacement cost is negligible vs. gearbox removal labour) [11].
7. Set backlash to **0.1–0.3 mm** for industrial mill-drive gearboxes; measure with dial gauge at minimum 8 positions around the circumference [4][6][11].
8. Verify tooth contact pattern with **Prussian blue compound** — contact must be centred on tooth face, covering **>70% face width and >60% tooth height** [4][6][11].
9. **Run-in at low load before returning to full drive load** [4][6].

---

## 6. Spare Procurement

| Action | Part | Description | Status | Lead Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ORDER NOW** | GEAR-WHL-M20 | Custom large-module gear wheel M20+ (HSM mill drive) — Flender / Renk OEM | Out of stock | **36 weeks** [6] |
| **ISSUE FROM STORE** | BRG-GBX-SET | Gearbox bearing set | 1 unit on hand | Immediate [6] |

**Total parts cost: INR 10,395,750** [6].

> Per recurrence-prevention protocol: raise the GEAR-WHL-M20 procurement order immediately — the 36-week lead means early ordering is the **only** way to avoid extended downtime on a future gear fracture event [9].

---

|---|---|

| Unplanned downtime | **168 hours (7 days)** [1] |
| Estimated production loss | **USD 600,000 (INR 50,100,000)** [1] |

The USD 600k point estimate reflects a ~7-day swap of the custom gear wheel plus secondary-damage repair; the range extends to USD 3M if secondary structural damage is found during teardown [1].

---

## 8. Recurrence Prevention

- Implement **monthly ferrographic oil analysis** on HSM.F1.GBX01 — ferrography detects gear spall particles 2–4 weeks before GMF alarm escalates to emergency level [9].
- Target continuous kidney-loop filtration to **ISO 4406 < 16/14/11** [9].
- Connect torque measurement to CMMS; auto-raise work order if torque exceeds **110% rated for >5 seconds** (cobble events are the primary tooth fatigue initiator) [9].
- Raise long-lead procurement for GEAR-WHL-M20 as soon as ferrous particle count first trends above **5 ppm** on any future sample — 36-week lead leaves no margin [9].
